MutSeqR: Development, Release & Versioning Guide

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

How MutSeqR is developed, versioned, and released. MutSeqR is a Bioconductor-managed package: it lives in two repositories and the release process is partly run by the Bioconductor team, so a few rules here are Bioconductor policy, not house style. Read §3 and §5 before your first push to Bioconductor.

1. The two repositories

Repo Remote URL Role
GitHub origin github.com/EHSRB-BSRSE-Bioinformatics/MutSeqR Development: branches, PRs, CI, pkgdown, GitHub Releases
Bioconductor upstream git@git.bioconductor.org:packages/MutSeqR.git (SSH) Canonical package; source of BiocManager::install() 
feature branch ─PR─> github devel ─PR─> github main ─push─> Bioc devel
                                                              │
                                                              │ twice a year, done BY
                                                              │ THE BIOCONDUCTOR TEAM
                                                              ▼
                                                    Bioc RELEASE_3_XX (even y)

Key facts about the Bioconductor side (see Git version control):

  • Only devel and the current RELEASE_X_Y branch exist and are writable. No new branches, no tags, no force-pushes on that server.
  • Releases are not git tags. A release = the RELEASE_X_Y branch plus the Bioc team’s version-bump commits. (Our GitHub tags are for local traceability only; they do nothing for the Bioc process.)
  • Pushing is only accepted as a fast-forward. If you’re behind, merge upstream/devel back first (§7).

2. Branch model

Branch Where Version Purpose
devel GitHub tracks main Feature staging: feature branches PR here, then here → main. Keep it current with main (git merge main into it after merges)
main GitHub and Bioc devel (kept in sync) odd y (e.g. 1.1.z) The push line: 1:1 with Bioc devel. Everything user-facing-next-release flows through here
RELEASE_3_XX Bioc even y (e.g. 1.0.z) Current release. Cherry-picks only (§6). No feature work, no merges
v1.0.0-Bioc3.23 GitHub tag + Release — Traceability marker per Bioc release; triggers the pkgdown workflow

Consequences:

  • End users install from Bioconductor, so “clean main” is for us: it is exactly the state we push upstream.
  • There is no GitHub mirror of RELEASE_X_Y; the release state is visible via the tag and on the Bioc server.

3. Versioning (Bioconductor policy)

From the version numbering rules:

  • Versions are x.y.z. y is even in release, odd in devel. 0.99.z was the pre-1.0 signal; MutSeqR’s first Bioc release (3.23) converted 0.99.11 → 1.0.0 (release) / 1.1.0 (devel).
  • Authors increment z by 1 for work pushed to the devel line. Commits without a z bump do not propagate to BiocManager::install().
  • y (and x) are bumped mechanically by the Bioc team at every release, for every package — release → next even y, devel → next odd y, z reset to 0. There is no per-package judgment about whether a bump is “deserved”: x.y encodes the release cycle, not the scale of change. (Bioc versions are not SemVer; NEWS.md + our release tags are the user-facing “what changed” channel.)
  • The only author-driven bump: setting y = 99 in devel signals “major changes” — the next release then converts x.99.z → (x+1).0.0. Use only when you actually ship breaking changes.
  • We never bump x/y ourselves, except the one-time y = 99 choice above. Our invariant to maintain: GitHub main == Bioc devel (they differ from the release by design — odd vs even y).
  • ⚠️ The x.x.9000 devel convention is a CRAN convention. Do not use it here — it violates the even/odd-y policy.

4. Everyday development

Use Pixi, Bash, and Docker for the shared Linux validation environment. It extends the official bioconductor/bioconductor_docker:devel image with the package’s dependencies, the exact roxygen2 version declared in DESCRIPTION, and LaTeX tools for the PDF manual. No host R or TeX installation is needed. On Windows, run these commands from WSL with Docker integration enabled. The manifest currently supports Linux and Intel macOS; Apple Silicon users need an Intel environment/emulation for this manifest.

# From a fresh clone: build the image if needed, then run the same gate as CI.
pixi run --locked -e container validate

# Before shipping: also require NEWS.md to name the DESCRIPTION version.
pixi run --locked -e container release-check

# Container diagnostics and individual checks.
pixi run -e container bioc-devel-info
pixi run -e container bioc-devel-test
pixi run -e container bioc-devel-check
pixi run -e container bioc-devel-bioccheck
pixi run -e container bioc-devel-shell
pixi run -e container bioc-devel-build  # refresh the moving devel base/dependencies

The container Pixi environment has no R dependencies; it calls the Docker engine already installed on your machine. The first run builds mutseqr-bioc-devel:local. Later runs reuse it; changes to DESCRIPTION or the Dockerfile automatically trigger a rebuild. Explicitly run bioc-devel-build to refresh the moving devel image even when those files have not changed. MUTSEQR_BIOC_DEVEL_IMAGE can override the local image tag.

Validation copies the current source tree, including uncommitted edits, into a temporary container workspace. Generated documentation, README output, and test plots cannot modify your checkout. Check logs are saved under .validation/, which is ignored by Git and excluded from the package. The interactive shell also uses a temporary copy; edits inside it disappear on exit.

validate runs documentation and README freshness, pkgdown reference coverage, unit tests, full R CMD check (including vignettes and the indexed PDF manual), and BiocCheck, stopping on the first failing gate. R CMD check fails on errors, warnings, or notes. BiocCheck uses its quit-with-status policy; its advisory warnings and notes still need review. release-check first requires the top NEWS heading to be exactly # MutSeqR <DESCRIPTION Version>, then runs the same validation gates. A passing gate covers these automated checks; external services and optional workflows still need appropriate review.

GitHub’s Bioconductor validation workflow runs this same Dockerfile, scripts, and pixi run --locked -e container validate on pull requests and pushes to main. It caches image layers and uploads .validation/ logs. A separate native Windows R-devel job checks platform compatibility and skips the PDF manual. The devel image and package repositories move over time, so a cached local image can differ from a fresh CI build; refresh it before investigating an environment discrepancy. Image/R/Bioconductor versions are printed in logs. If branch protection required the old documentation jobs or Linux matrix job, replace those required checks with Bioconductor devel (Linux).

For fast editing and tests without Docker, the default Pixi environment provides native R, tooling, and package dependencies via conda-forge/Bioconda:

pixi install --locked
pixi run test
pixi run document
pixi run check-docs
pixi run check-readme
pixi run check-reference
pixi run install-hooks
pixi run check       # full check; requires a host LaTeX installation
pixi run bioccheck

pixi run validate and pixi run release-check also use the container, but the explicit -e container form avoids installing the native R environment. Native PDF checks use R_RD4PDF=times,hyper to avoid the optional Inconsolata font; they do not install TeX automatically. Container PDF checks use the same font setting with TeX provisioned when the image is built.

The individual native freshness tasks compare output before and after the run. If they report changed files, review and commit the generated output, then rerun. The container runs these tasks on its temporary copy; regenerate stale files with the native document task or render README.Rmd locally before committing.

Run pixi run install-hooks once after cloning to enable the version-controlled pre-commit hook. When a commit includes R/roxygen sources or README sources, the hook runs the corresponding freshness check. If generation changes an output, review and stage the generated files before committing again. The hook is a fast local guard; CI remains the authoritative validation. In an exceptional case, Git’s standard --no-verify option bypasses the local hook.

Feature flow:

  1. git checkout -b feature/... main (or off devel — either is fine, PRs land on devel)
  2. Develop; PR → devel (CI: R-CMD-check on all PRs).
  3. PR devel → main when the batch is ready to ship.
  4. After the merge: bump devel current with main.
  5. Push the batch to Bioconductor (§5).

NEWS.md: keep the top entry at or ahead of the current devel version. One entry per release at minimum; the release ritual (§5) enforces it.

5. Pushing work to Bioconductor

Do this after merging to main, when the batch is ready:

pixi run -e container prepare-release  # bump z, finalize NEWS, validate that version
git diff -- DESCRIPTION NEWS.md
git add DESCRIPTION NEWS.md
git commit -m "chore: prepare next Bioconductor version"
git push origin main
git push upstream main:devel    # 'upstream' = git.bioconductor.org; writes to its 'devel'

Verify it landed:

  • Next day’s devel build report shows your commit; BiocManager::install("MutSeqR", version = "devel") gives you the new 1.1.z.
  • If the push is rejected (non-fast-forward): git fetch upstream, git merge upstream/devel, resolve, then push again.

prepare-release requires a clean worktree, increments z, converts the top # MutSeqR (development version) NEWS heading to that version, and runs release-check. Input and prepared metadata are checked before either file is replaced; an invalid NEWS heading leaves both files unchanged. If the subsequent release-check fails, the metadata edits remain available for review and correction; rerun release-check after fixing the failure. It never commits or pushes. You can instead edit Version and NEWS yourself and run release-check directly.

Run the isolated release-preparation regression tests with bash scripts/test-prepare-release.sh (requires Bash and Git, not R or Docker).

6. Hotfixes to the released version

Users of the current release (e.g. 1.0.0 on Bioc 3.23) do not see the devel line. A user-facing hotfix means cherry-picking to the release branch:

  1. Fix on the devel line as usual (PR → main, z bump, push to upstream devel) so the fix also rides the next release.
  2. Cherry-pick the fix commit (not the version-bump commit) onto upstream/RELEASE_3_XX, bump its z separately (e.g. 1.0.0 → 1.0.1), commit, git push upstream RELEASE_3_XX.
  3. Only the current release branch is writable; for older releases, email maintainer@bioconductor.org.
  4. Never merge devel → release; cherry-picks only.
  5. Note the fix in NEWS.md under the release version.

7. When Bioconductor cuts a release (≈ twice a year)

The Bioc team branches RELEASE_3_XX and bumps versions on both their branches (devel: even→odd y, e.g. 1.1.0 → 1.3.0 for the cycle after 3.24… see the table in the Bioc docs). Our ritual afterwards:

  1. git fetch upstream
  2. Merge upstream/devel into local main (usually fast-forward) → git push origin main.
  3. Tag + GitHub Release on the released commit: v1.2.0-Bioc3.24 → release notes in NEWS → triggers pkgdown.
  4. Update pins for the new Bioc cycle:
    • pixi.toml: update r-base when Bioconda publishes packages for the new Bioconductor/R cycle
    • pixi run bioc-devel-build: pull and rebuild the moving devel image
  5. Bump devel staging branch current with main.

8. Quick reference / troubleshooting

Symptom Cause / fix
git push upstream main:devel rejected You’re behind Bioc: git fetch upstream && git merge upstream/devel, then push
Change pushed but BiocManager::install() doesn’t see it No z bump in DESCRIPTION (Bioc only serves bumped commits)
ssh -T git@git.bioconductor.org → permission denied Register your SSH key in the BiocCredentials app; a correct key prints your package list with R W next to MutSeqR
Pushing to upstream a branch other than devel/RELEASE_3_XX Not possible by policy — do it via GitHub + the flows above
“Should I use 1.2.9000 on devel?” No — that’s CRAN. Here: odd y, z bumps (§3)
R version / Bioc version mismatch in pixi pixi.toml pins r-base to the current Bioc cycle’s R; update at each release (§7)

9. Open items

  • Pull requests run the shared Bioconductor container validation and native Windows R-devel compatibility checks. The pkgdown site continues to publish on release; pull requests validate the reference without publishing it.
  • Optional CI gate: PR touching R/ must change DESCRIPTION Version and NEWS.md.
